title: Transcription pause and elongation regulators mediate somatic hypermutation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened all 13 supplementary/source-data spreadsheets from the article page (1.7 MB total, 70 sheets, 41,616 non-empty cells). Supplementary Table 1 = 38 rows of PCR primers; Supplementary Table 2 = exactly two DNA sequences (one IGH-V, one IGK-V amplicon reference). Every Source Data sheet is figure-level summary values: e.g. Fig. 1d is 3 target loci x 4 treatments x 3 replicates of point-mutation frequency; the biggest sheet (Extended Data Fig. 4j) is 18,520 bare numbers in 5 columns ('All genes', 'Cluster 1-4') with no gene identifiers and no text anywhere. Confirmed via NCBI E-utilities that PubMed ID 42816608 has no linked GEO, SRA, BioProject or BioSample records, and that BioProject PRJNA1337487 exists with 907 SRA (Sequence Read Archive) runs of raw reads.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The Methods description of the assays (amplicon mutation sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq X, CUT&RUN-seq at ~20 million reads per sample, TT-TimeLapse-seq at ~30 million reads per sample) and of the custom alignment/Pysamstats pipeline used to call per-position mutations. I did not download any raw sequencing run. I did not verify that PRJNA1337487 contains all three assay types, only that it holds 907 runs.

a1_downloadable.note: All supplementary and source-data files download freely (verified, article is CC BY-NC-ND); BioProject PRJNA1337487 is public with 907 SRA runs, no login or access application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: KILLER. No prediction target is a column anywhere. Per-position or per-gene mutation rates exist only inside 907 raw FASTQ read files and would have to be constructed by rerunning the authors' alignment plus Pysamstats pipeline; no processed mutation table, peak file or bigwig track is deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked files: two amplicon reference sequences are given in Supplementary Table 2, so sequence inputs exist for those two loci; chromatin/PolII inputs exist only as raw reads.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked files: sheets carry only figure labels such as 'total mutation frequency' or bare numbers; units (fraction of bases, percent IgM loss, fold change, cell number) live on the figure axes, not in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in files: 69 of 70 sheets have <=38 rows of replicate summary values; the single 18,520-row sheet is an unlabelled distribution for a violin plot with no identifiers or features, so it cannot form rows of a feature/label table.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.002 GB of spreadsheets, versus hundreds of GB for the 907 raw SRA runs
a6_fits_laptop.note: The usable route would require downloading and aligning 907 raw sequencing runs (CUT&RUN and TT-TimeLapse-seq at 20-30 million reads each), which breaks both the no-raw-sequencing rule and the 16 GB laptop budget.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Replicate counts in the sheets match the figure captions I read (e.g. n = 3 per condition in Fig. 1d, n = 3/4/6 in Fig. 1i).

a8_label_provenance.note: The numbers are direct amplicon-sequencing measurements of mutation frequency, not another model's output; this is the one Part A item the dataset passes cleanly.

existing_models.name: DeepSHM (convolutional neural network predicting somatic hypermutation rate from k-mer DNA sequence context, iScience 2022, PubMed ID 35036866)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the search summary: reported improved accuracy over earlier k-mer mutability models (such as the S5F 5-mer model) using 5-21 nucleotide contexts; split not verified.

existing_models.name: Interpretable deep learning of immunoglobulin variable-region hypermutation (E-box motif study, 2024, found via search; PubMed Central PMC11165027)

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 or HyenaDNA (DNA language models) would be the natural fit for per-base mutability from sequence
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for two short amplicons, but there is no label table to fit a head to
backbone.licence: open weights (not assessed in detail, project rejected earlier)

integration.partner_dataset: Observed Antibody Space / published B-cell receptor repertoire mutation profiles
integration.join_key: IGHV gene name and position in the IMGT numbering scheme
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does pausing-factor occupancy explain where hypermutation lands beyond local sequence motifs? - unanswerable here because neither the occupancy tracks nor the per-position mutation rates are deposited in processed form.

controls.positive_control: A model should recover the textbook WRC/AID hotspot preference (W = A or T, R = A or G) seen in the paper's own hotspot analysis.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle mutation labels across positions; mutation-frequency signal should collapse to the per-locus mean.
controls.external_validation: Public B-cell receptor repertoire datasets with per-position mutation counts (e.g. Observed Antibody Space) exist, but the join was not attempted.

honest_claim_h3: With only figure-level summary values, a model could at best claim to interpolate mutation frequencies across four degron conditions at three amplicon loci in one human germinal-centre B-cell line - a claim no one needs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use local DNA sequence and transcription-pausing signals to predict where antibody genes acquire point mutations during antibody maturation.
plain_idea.train_on: Ideally each base position in immunoglobulin variable regions, described by its surrounding DNA sequence and by RNA polymerase II pausing and NELF/MLLT1 occupancy; the number of such labelled positions in downloadable form is effectively zero (only two amplicon reference sequences and figure-level averages are deposited).
plain_idea.predict: The mutation frequency at each base, measured by deep amplicon sequencing of genomic DNA from germinal-centre B cells; here that measurement exists only inside 907 raw sequencing runs, not as a table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Antibody engineers and B-cell immunologists want to know why mutations concentrate where they do; linking pausing factors to mutation position would move the field past pure sequence-motif models. None of that is testable from what this paper deposits.

more_or_better_data.why: The downloadable data is a few hundred replicate averages at three loci in one cell line, far smaller than the millions of mutated repertoire sequences that DeepSHM-style models were trained on.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate measurements exist per condition, but with only three loci there are nowhere near enough groups to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: DeepSHM is a 2022 convolutional network on k-mer context with no pretrained DNA backbone, so it is probably beatable - but not with this paper's data, which contains no per-position labels.

guaranteed_improvement.why: We cannot run DeepSHM as a baseline on the same split, and the chromatin features that would be added are not deposited in processed form; both required conditions fail.

ml_idea: Considered: predict per-base somatic hypermutation rate along immunoglobulin variable regions from DNA sequence context plus NELF/PolII/MLLT1 occupancy, and test whether pausing-factor signal adds information over AID hotspot motifs. Rejected because no per-position mutation table and no processed occupancy track is deposited.

effort.compute_note: Spreadsheet working set measured on disk (1.7 MB). The only route to a label table is realigning 907 raw SRA runs including genome-wide CUT&RUN and TT-TimeLapse-seq, which is cluster-scale and was not attempted; hence the other estimates are null.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open every source-data spreadsheet and count labelled rows - done: 69 of 70 sheets have at most 38 rows, and the one 18,520-row sheet has no identifiers.

verdict_reason: A2 fails, verified in the files: the only deposited tables are figure-level replicate averages (70 sheets, <=38 rows each) plus one 18,520-value unlabelled distribution, so any mutation-rate label would have to be rebuilt from 907 raw sequencing runs, which also fails A5 and A6. Excellent biology, no model-ready data.
